NDT software in Denver: Front Range work covers very different sectors

Denver has no single dominant NDT customer, and that is what makes running an inspection company here hard. North and east of the city, the Denver-Julesburg (DJ) Basin keeps midstream operators, gas processing plants, compressor stations and gathering lines busy. That work comes under the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission (formerly the COGCC) and, for pipelines, PHMSA and the Colorado Public Utilities Commission. In Commerce City, the Suncor refinery, Colorado's only operating refinery, drives turnaround and routine plant inspection. Along the south and west metro, the aerospace sector adds precision work: Lockheed Martin Space near Littleton, United Launch Alliance headquartered in Centennial, BAE Systems' space business in Boulder and Broomfield (formerly Ball Aerospace), and the machine shops and fabricators that supply them.

On top of that, the Front Range construction market generates steady structural steel weld inspection on buildings, bridges and transit work, usually visual and UT against AWS D1.1 for special inspection programmes. Utilities and power plants across Colorado add boiler and piping work. Boilers and pressure vessels are regulated by the state Division of Oil and Public Safety, and radioactive materials licensing runs through CDPHE, since Colorado is an Agreement State.

A Denver NDT contractor may therefore send a VT/UT inspector to a downtown high-rise, a PAUT crew to a DJ Basin compressor station and a PT technician to an aerospace shop on the same morning. The Atlantis ERP solution is built for that kind of spread.

ERP for NDT companies in Denver: the short answer

An ERP for NDT companies in Denver should let one office manage construction, oil and gas, refinery and aerospace work without four separate paperwork systems. The Atlantis ERP keeps certifications, calibration, dispatch, reports, procedures, quotes and invoices in one system, configured for your company by an ASNT NDT Level III.

The main thing a Denver company gains is consistency across very different clients. A general contractor's special inspection programme, a refinery's contractor QA manual and an aerospace customer's purchase order all ask the same underlying questions. Was the technician qualified? Was the instrument calibrated? Which procedure revision did you use? Who reviewed the report? When every job answers those questions the same way in the ERP, audits get shorter and fewer reports come back for rework.

For small NDT companies in Denver, the second gain is not needing to hire an administrator just to keep certs, calibration and invoicing aligned. The system raises the warnings and the team acts on them.

NDT reporting software for structural steel, plant and aerospace work

NDT reporting software for Denver has to produce a structural weld report that a building official accepts, a refinery report that meets the owner's format and an aerospace report with full traceability. The Atlantis ERP includes 17 report types: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography. Each has its own numbering sequence.

On construction work, VT and UT reports carry weld and job lines with defect type and orientation, plus references to drawing, WPS, contract and applicable standard. On refinery and midstream work, RT reports record source, technique, IQI type and placement, and PAUT and TOFD reports hold setup detail including focal laws. UT thickness reports record readings by direction, and PMI, hardness and ferrite reports cover alloy and weld checks. For aerospace shops, PT, MT and ECT reports capture method, developer, particle type and technique. Every report ends with acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks.

Reports move from draft through in progress, review and approved to sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures. Where a third party or authorised inspector signs, their name and signature are captured too. Versioned company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML carry your logo and header, and Excel templates fill automatically by mapping fields to cells, which is handy when a general contractor wants their own log format.

In the mountains and out on the eastern plains, signal drops. The offline field app keeps drafts and photos on the device and syncs later. See Digital Twin Reporting Software and the NDT Reports app for more.

Technician certification tracking for Denver's construction, plant and aerospace clients

Technician certification tracking in Denver means holding several kinds of qualification against one person and knowing which one a job needs. The Certificates app records scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level, method, certifying body, industry sector, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT hours, training hours, exam results and attachments. Welding inspector credentials and aerospace qualifications can be recorded under the other scheme, alongside the technician's NDT certifications.

Status updates automatically to active, expiring soon (90 days), expired or revoked. Vision tests are tracked on their own, with near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic and expiry. Examination sheets store general, specific and practical scores against a configurable passing score. Certificate templates per scheme set validity, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours.

Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before a cert or vision test expires, and email alerts go to recipients you choose, with your own look-ahead and resend settings. Timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid. Company certifications, such as ISO 9001, sit alongside with their own alert days, so the documents a Denver general contractor's QA team or an aerospace buyer asks for are always current.

Calibration management software for Front Range instrument fleets

Calibration management software for a Denver contractor needs to show instrument condition as well as calibration dates. Kit moves between heated shops, cold job sites and high-altitude mountain work, and it takes a beating. The Asset Management app tracks each instrument, probe and accessory by serial number, with type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle status: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed.

The issue and return workflow records condition when an instrument leaves and when it comes back, with supervisor and manager approval. If a UT set comes back from a January job in the foothills with a cracked cable, the record shows who had it. The maintenance log covers preventive and corrective maintenance, repair, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacement, with condition before and after.

Calibration records hold provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result and next due date. The certificate register tracks the lab's accreditation number and the PDF, marks each certificate valid, expiring or expired, and sends expiry alerts. Aerospace customers often ask about calibration lab accreditation, and the Purchase app records calibration labs as a vendor type with accreditation details. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer and MT particles carry reorder levels and low-stock flags.

Crew dispatch software for DJ Basin, metro and mountain jobs

Crew dispatch software for Denver has to account for travel that the map understates. The I-70 corridor in winter, a spread-out metro and DJ Basin sites out past Greeley all stretch a technician's day. The Team Assignments app moves each job from planned to dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates.

The technician availability calendar tracks assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days and blocks overlaps. Double-booking a technician, or the same instrument serial number, is blocked, and the dispatcher is warned when assigned equipment is out of calibration. Calendar, kanban and list views show each technician's current assignment, utilisation and next available date. That makes it easier to fit short construction visits around longer plant jobs.

The Fleet app records vehicle purpose, whether the vehicle can carry radioactive sources, its transport licence number and expiry, and its assignment to a project and driver with dates and mileage. Time Off approvals feed the same availability calendar. Timesheets record travel as its own work type, so the hours spent getting to a mountain site are visible and billable where your contract allows.

Procedures and document control for Denver inspection companies

Denver clients, especially aerospace and refinery owners, will ask which procedure revision was used on a given job. The Procedures app holds a register with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard, acceptance criteria and body text or file. Methods covered include UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, PAUT, LT, AE, hardness, PMI, CR and DR.

The workflow runs from draft to submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejection reasons and archiving. Approved revisions lock, and every revision keeps a snapshot. An AI-assisted first draft can help your Level III start a new procedure, but they still review and approve it. Approvers get reminders by email. Project tasks carry procedure and WPS references, so the procedure used on each weld or component is on record.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Denver inspection companies

NDT quoting and invoicing software needs to handle the billing styles Denver clients use: day rates for plant work, visit-based billing for construction special inspection, and job-based pricing for aerospace shop work. Any structure beyond the standard fields is configured during implementation. Atlantis ERP quotations carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT service products flagged by method and category, a global discount option and a branded PDF. Clients can accept and sign online, and the quote converts to a sales order.

Invoices carry project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals. Lines show cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Cost centres let you see whether construction, oil and gas or aerospace work is carrying the business. Approved timesheet hours with billable flag and rate multiplier feed billing. The financial dashboard reports revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA and outstanding invoices over 12 months, and Expenses handles per diems and field costs re-billed to jobs.

Inspection management software in Denver: dashboards, CRM and integrations

Inspection management software gives a Denver operations manager one screen for the things that cause trouble: calibration due and overdue, certs expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue for return. These NDT KPI dashboards sit next to the financial dashboard.

The CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days, and scores each lead from 0 to 100. Construction bids, midstream enquiries and aerospace RFQs can each run their own drip sequence. The Business Cards app turns a photo of a card from a Denver trade event into a lead in one click.

The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. The scope is agreed during implementation, whether that is your accounting package or a client portal.

Affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Denver: implementation

An affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Denver is configured to your mix of work rather than to one industry template. The Atlantis ERP is quoted on request and set up by Atlantis NDT.

  1. Review your work mix. We look at your written practice, construction, plant and aerospace report formats, and how each client is billed.
  2. Load records. We import technicians, certifications, vision tests, instruments, calibration certificates, procedures, vehicles and clients.
  3. Configure templates and cost centres. We set up report templates per client type and cost centres per business line.
  4. Field pilot. Crews run live jobs on the offline app while the office handles dispatch and approvals in the ERP.
  5. Integrate and train. We scope the API connections and train office staff and your Level III.

For new hires, Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training with an eLearning portal and the Practical NDT 3D simulator. For owners who want inspection data shown in 3D, see Atlantis Digital Twins. Book a Denver-focused demo.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a Denver company doing construction and plant inspection?

The best fit handles construction weld reports and plant NDT reports in the same system, with shared certification and calibration records. The Atlantis ERP supports 17 report types with per-client templates, so one company can serve both markets from one database.

Can the ERP produce reports in a general contractor's or owner's own format?

Yes. Company templates are versioned in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML, and Excel templates fill automatically by mapping report fields to cells.

Does it track welding inspector and aerospace qualifications as well as NDT certifications?

Yes. Other qualifications are recorded under the other scheme, with dates, sector and attachments, next to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 certifications. Atlantis training itself is SNT-TC-1A-based only.

How is the Atlantis ERP priced for Denver inspection companies?

It is quoted on request, based on team size, apps and integrations, and positioned to be affordable for small and mid-sized NDT companies. Request a quote.

Will the field app work in the mountains or on the eastern plains?

Yes. The offline field app stores drafts and photos locally and syncs when coverage returns.

Can it integrate with our accounting system?

Yes. The open REST API supports integrations with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped during implementation.
